classification.difficultyReason: Requires recognising similar right triangles within composite figures and combining corresponding-side ratios with Pythagoras.

spec.description: Right triangle ADC with altitude DB to horizontal AC; A, B, C occur in order. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: AD perpendicular DC; DB perpendicular AC; AB=9; DB=12; no units supplied.

answer.short:
$AD=15$, $DC=20$, $BC=16$.

Use Pythagoras and proportional sides of the similar right triangles.
answer.worked:
In right triangle $ABD$, by Pythagoras:
$$\begin{align*}AD^2&=9^2+12^2\\AD^2&=225\\AD&=15\end{align*}$$
$\angle ABD=\angle DBC=90^\circ$ and $\angle BAD=\angle BDC$ because both are complementary to $\angle ADB$. Hence $\triangle ABD\sim\triangle DBC$ by AAA.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{BC}{DB}&=\frac{DB}{AB}\\\frac{BC}{12}&=\frac{12}{9}\\BC&=16\end{align*}$$
In right triangle $DBC$:
$$\begin{align*}DC^2&=12^2+16^2\\DC^2&=400\\DC&=20\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Rectangle BADC, diagonal BD, and perpendicular AM meeting BD at M. All four corner squares and the square at M are retained. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: CD=20; AD=15; AM perpendicular BD; no units supplied.

answer.short:
$AM=12$, $BM=16$, $DM=9$.

Find $BD$ using Pythagoras, then use similar right triangles.
answer.worked:
Opposite sides of the rectangle are equal, so $AB=20$. In right triangle $ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}BD^2&=20^2+15^2\\BD^2&=625\\BD&=25\end{align*}$$
$\angle BAD=\angle BMA=90^\circ$ and $\angle ABD=\angle MBA$ because $M$ lies on $BD$. Hence $\triangle ABD\sim\triangle MBA$ by AAA.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AM}{AD}&=\frac{AB}{BD}\\\frac{AM}{15}&=\frac{20}{25}\\AM&=12\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{BM}{AB}&=\frac{AB}{BD}\\\frac{BM}{20}&=\frac{20}{25}\\BM&=16\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}DM&=BD-BM\\DM&=25-16\\DM&=9\end{align*}$$
